glance_takeaway: This page explains how diffusion image generators (Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, DALL-E 3, Flux) all work: a fixed forward process gradually destroys an image into noise over ~1,000 steps, a network learns to undo one small step at a time, and generation runs the process backwards starting from pure random noise. All the variants — DDIM, latent diffusion, distillation, flow matching — exist to make sampling cheaper: naive sampling needs ~1,000 network passes, DDIM cuts it to 20-50, and latent-space diffusion (~48x fewer values) is what put Stable Diffusion on consumer GPUs. It also stresses two things it never does: generation doesn't start from an existing photo, and the model doesn't store copies of its training images.

strengths: Perfect fact coverage: all 15 ground-truth facts land, including the fiddly ones (10-20% prompt dropout, 786,432 vs 16,384 numbers, DDIM-as-ODE-discretization, memorization-exception nuance).
The above-the-fold layer is genuinely self-sufficient: hero diagram + four stat tiles + misconception banner deliver T1, T2 (partially), and T3 in one screen.
Honest, purposeful graphics — the step-count chart is a real log-scale with correctly placed bars and a retrain-vs-no-retrain color legend; the CFG vector diagram matches the extrapolation formula.
weaknesses: The fourth takeaway (guidance) is below the fold except for a terse 's = 7.5' tile that a glancing reader can miss — my own glance takeaway did not register it.
No table of contents or anchor links on a 13-section page; wayfinding relies on scrolling past numbered kickers.

The interactive CFG slider carries some content (zone descriptions) that is invisible in any static rendering or print; the key numbers are duplicated in the scale labels, mitigating but not eliminating this.
evaluator_notes: Accuracy is formulaic: 15/15 conveyed, 0 distorted, 0 contradicted -> 10.0. Glance scored strictly from the recorded takeaway: T1 and T3 fully landed, T2 mostly (missed the 10-20 and 1-4 tiers), T4 missed entirely -> 7.5. Depth is strong for the briefed audience (jargon defined inline, glossary, misconceptions section directly serves the brief's debunking goal), held below 9 because 13 sections is a lot for a 2-3 minute read. Verified the log-scale bar chart geometry against its axis (180px=1, 690px=1000): all bars are numerically correct. Caveats present throughout: modest quality loss (DDIM), compression bottleneck (VAE), quality/diversity cost (distillation), artifact regime (CFG), memorization exception.
